history.period: 1988 CE, with CONFLICT: some sources say 1977
history.summary: Modern temple in the Morar area of Gwalior dedicated to Surya (the Sun God), built by industrialist G.D. Birla - most sources say 1988, though at least one says 1977 (CONFLICT), and one site says 1788, which is clearly an error. It is a replica of the Konark Sun Temple in Odisha, built in chariot form with 24 wheels (the hours of the day) drawn by seven horses (the days of the week), reportedly ringed by 365 deity images. The exterior is red sandstone while the interior is white marble; windows are said to be aligned so sunlight falls on the Sun image from dawn to dusk. Opening hours CONFLICT widely across sources (verify before visiting).

name: Sun Temple (Surya Mandir)
town_description: Morar is a township in the Gwalior metropolitan area of northern Madhya Pradesh, formerly a British-era cantonment known for its orderly military layout and wide roads. It lies east of the historic Gwalior city core and houses hospitals, schools and the Birla-built Sun Temple. Morar is functionally part of Gwalior city; CSV town 'Gwalior' is the broader city.
